value.rationale: Spanning-tree count is a canonical global complexity invariant for a recent dependent random-graph model. The beta-posterior law drives non-self-averaging \(O(n)\) behavior of log tree count, while a nontrivial conditional \(\sqrt n\) Gaussian limit has an explicit variance including \(\pi^2/3\) at p=1/2. This is a motivated refinement of spectral and graphon knowledge; no paper-sized generalization is claimed.
